<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Data and strange claims</p><h1>Cage-free vs. caged hens in the US</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>12 Apr 2023</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>Some time ago, when the fall semester began, I enrolled in a Data Science Lab course. One assignment was to make a TidyTuesday contribution and present it in class. This was one of my first respectable attempts at visualizing data.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>How did the number of cage-free hens change relative to traditionally housed hens over the observed period?</p><h2>The plot</h2><p>The analysis filters for table eggs, joins the reported cage-free percentages to the total number of hens, and turns the result into a stacked time-series view.</p><p>Kinda messy. Still worth plotting.</p></article></main>
